title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Grothendieck is working out the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}, meaning the stratification of the Deligne–Mumford–Knudsen compactification by the normal-crossings boundary divisor. Alongside this he is building a general formalism for 'local stratifications'. On the previous page, D_{Δ_r} is the space of local flags of length r, Σ_x = {x ∈ X̄_{i_0} ⊂ X̄_{i_1} ⊂ … ⊂ X̄_{i_r}}, where the X̄_{i} are germs at x of closures of local strata. He asks whether the Segal-type map (303), D_{Δ_2} → D_{Δ_1} ×_{D_{Δ_0}} D_{Δ_1}, is a homeomorphism. If it is, the stratified space defines a topological category: the objects form D_{Δ_0} (the space of local strata, i.e. pairs (point, germ of stratum closure through it)), the arrows form D_{Δ_1} (local flags), and source, target and composition are the obvious maps. D_{Δ_•} is then the nerve of this category.

This page, (304): consider the simplicial 'first vertex' map σ: D_{Δ_r} → D_{Δ_0}, which sends a chain of arrows to its source. Grothendieck asserts that σ is finite étale (a finite covering map) over an open part D*_{Δ_0}. The margin says that D*_{Δ_r} is defined as σ^{-1}(D*_{Δ_0}). Presumably D*_{Δ_0} is the 'strict' part, where x lies in the open stratum X_{i_0} itself and not merely in its closure. Over such a point, the fibre of σ is the finite set of chains of local strata whose closures contain the given local stratum near x. The claim says this finite set varies locally constantly along the stratum.

The parenthetical NB, partly illegible, says roughly this: in a special ('évasé'?) case the space is just a finite union over D_{Δ_0}, but that is 'a very special fact', owed to the strata being topological manifolds.

He then adds a second statement, left unfinished. The local ordered structure of D*_{Δ_r} over D*_{Δ_0} — the poset of local strata containing a given local stratum — is itself locally constant, i.e. it forms a locally constant sheaf of finite posets on each stratum. The next page continues: for normal crossings this poset is the power set of a finite set (the local branches, i.e. the nodes for M̄_{g,ν}). This already fails for three concurrent branches in the plane, where the central stratum's poset is not a Boolean lattice.

What this serves: these are the combinatorial-topological invariants of the stratification at infinity. Each stratum carries a locally constant poset of incident local strata; for the DM boundary these are the dual-graph / edge-subset data, and they make up a topological nerve. This is groundwork for describing tubular neighbourhoods and the 'élémentary types' (the boundary structure of M̄_{g,ν} in the spirit of the Teichmüller tower of the Esquisse).
errors: Gap: finite étaleness of σ over D*_{Δ_0}, and local constancy of the poset of incident local strata, do not follow from the frontier condition alone. The number of local branches of X̄_{i_1} along X_{i_0} can jump unless some equisingularity or local-triviality hypothesis holds (conical structure, Thom–Mather/Whitney). On the next page Grothendieck himself notes he has 'not yet used the local triviality hypothesis (p. 86 e))'. So either the claim tacitly uses it, or it is unproved at this point.
The status of the Segal condition (303) is only posed as a question on the previous page; the topological-category structure used here depends on it.
The parenthetical about the special case ('due to strata being topological manifolds') is too illegible to verify.

ideas.what: Space of local flags of a stratified space forming the nerve of a topological category (objects = local strata, arrows = local flags), with σ = first-vertex/source map.
ideas.modern_name: exit-path category / exit-path ∞-category of a stratified space (also the 'poset of strata' refined to local branches)
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (unpublished, 1990s), Treumann (2009), Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A), Ayala–Francis–Tanaka (2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 sketches 'dévissage of stratified structures' and tame topology only in general terms; this construction is not there.

ideas.what: Source map from r-chains of local strata to local strata is a finite covering over the open part of each stratum.
ideas.modern_name: finiteness/local constancy of incidence data along strata (constructibility of the exit-path category; link-branch covering)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in Whitney/Thom–Mather stratification theory; formalised in the exit-path literature

ideas.what: Locally constant sheaf of finite posets on each stratum, given by the local strata containing it; Boolean (power set) exactly in the normal-crossings case, failing for three concurrent branches.
ideas.modern_name: local incidence poset / normal-crossings (toroidal) combinatorics; dual-complex/cone-complex of the boundary of M̄_{g,n}

missed.claim: Grothendieck presents a stratified space as a topological category (strictly, a Segal-type topological nerve) built from local flags. Its source map is a finite covering over the strata. This is essentially an early, point-set version of the exit-path category, applied to the DM boundary of M_{g,ν}. It predates MacPherson's and Treumann's formulations and the later ∞-categorical treatments of moduli of curves.
missed.quote: D_{Δ_r} →σ D_{Δ_0} application simpliciale correspondant au "premier sommet" ... une application finie étale au dessus de D*_{Δ_0}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is historical credit for the stratified-space-as-category viewpoint (exit paths, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka). It also offers a strict topological-category model, with a Segal homeomorphism condition, for the boundary stratification of M̄_{g,n}. That model could be compared with the tropical/cone-complex description of the boundary.

deep.surprise_reason: The page belongs to a sequence where Grothendieck, apparently in the early 1980s, turns a local stratification into a topological category with nerve D_{Δ_•}. That is a recognisable precursor of exit-path categories, which are credited to MacPherson and Treumann and appear in Lurie's work much later. The page's own content (the finite-étale source map and the locally constant poset of incident strata) is routine given local triviality, and the main idea sits on the previous page. Hence notable but not startling.
transcription_corrections: 'dû[?] = que les faits que' likely reads 'dû au fait que les' — i.e. due to the fact that the strata are topological manifolds.
The margin note reads 'NB D*_{Δ_r} est l'image inverse de D*_{Δ_0}' (confirmed as the definition of D*_{Δ_r} via σ).

'Également le fait que la structure ordonnée locale des D*_{Δ_r} sur D*_{Δ_0} (structure de l'une des strates locales contenant une strate locale donnée) soit ...': the sentence is unfinished, and 'structure de simplexe' is struck out; it continues onto the next page ('... à l'une des parties d'un ens. fini [not 'fermé'], et spécial. aux croisements normaux').
'cas "évasé"' is uncertain; it may be another word, so the reading should be kept tentative.
